approved_differences.statement: No HTTP behavior difference is approved in this internal capability slice. Authentication, identity activity, snake-case projection and safe errors remain future operations-owned parity requirements.

forbidden_in_this_slice: HTTP controller, security matcher, role decision or rate limiter
users, user_subjects, public-bank snapshot or identity-policy lookup
locked, null-lock, empty-name, signed-ID or zero-question filtering
route parity delta or OpenAPI operation migration

catalog_application_contract.runtime_sql: one explicit four-column SELECT over subjects LEFT JOIN questions with COUNT(q.id), no predicates or binds, GROUP BY all subject facts and fixed s.id ASC ordering

result_semantics.cardinality: one row for every subjects row; no filters, limit or pagination
result_semantics.signed_id: the complete Java/PostgreSQL signed integer domain remains representable, including zero and negative historical keys
result_semantics.name: empty, whitespace-only and Unicode names remain exact
result_semantics.lock: true, false and null remain distinct; no primitive boolean or COALESCE is allowed
result_semantics.question_count: COUNT(q.id) is a nonnegative long; subjects with no matching questions remain present with zero
result_semantics.unassigned_or_orphan_questions: questions with null or nonmatching subject_id do not contribute to any subject count
result_semantics.failure: the original persistence exception propagates unchanged so operations can apply the reviewed HTTP policy

authentication.valid_administrator_bearer_only: 302 Location /login because the global Web gate blocks Bearer-only access
authentication.ordinary_session_plus_valid_administrato: 302 Location /login because the Bearer header bypasses the Web-session branch of the global gate

success_projection.locked_values: PostgreSQL JSON booleans are true/false/null; the pinned SQLite legacy capture observes 1/0/null and is explicitly a dialect observation
success_projection.question_count: JSON integer backed by SQL COUNT(q.id)

failure_semantics.database_failure_accept_any: 500 fixed generic Chinese HTML error page after one attempted inventory SELECT
failure_semantics.database_failure_accept_json: 500 generic safe JSON error envelope after one attempted inventory SELECT

cross_cutting_effects.subjects_fingerprint: all nine subjects columns remain unchanged for every case
cross_cutting_effects.questions_fingerprint: all fifteen questions columns remain unchanged for every case
cross_cutting_effects.session_activity: Session-only requests, including an eventually forbidden ordinary session, can update users.last_active once before authorization; this identity effect is outside the catalog primitive and separately ledgered
cross_cutting_effects.blocked_bearer_paths: anonymous, Bearer-only and Session-plus-Bearer redirect before business SQL
cross_cutting_effects.rate_limit: the route declares no route-specific limit; future operations must preserve the applicable global policy rather than invent one

query_plan_contract.environment: PostgreSQL 18.4 pinned digest with network none, parallel gather disabled and public synthetic data
query_plan_contract.interpretation: observational evidence only; it is not a production latency SLA, capacity claim, index recommendation or migration authorization

invariants: The catalog capability reads only catalog-owned subjects and questions and never consults identity visibility or public-bank projections.
Every invocation executes exactly one parameter-free SELECT and no DML, DDL or TEMP operation.
LEFT JOIN and COUNT(q.id) preserve every subject and emit zero for subjects without assigned questions.
All four subject facts preserve signed IDs, exact names and nullable lock values in strict signed ID ascending order.
No HTTP authentication, users.last_active behavior, snake-case projection, response envelope or safe-error translation enters catalog.
Persistence failures remain untranslated at the catalog boundary.
PostgreSQL 16.14 and 18.4 execute the same adapter SQL and preserve the same boundary values.
Synthetic query-plan indexes are observational only and authorize neither a production migration nor a production index.
The HTTP operation remains operations-owned and pending; this capability changes no route, OpenAPI migration status, module dependency or production traffic.

required_before_phase4h_route_migration: approve and machine-check the operations dependency on catalog::api
implement the complete global gate, subject-admin role and users.last_active behavior
project isLocked and questionCount to exact is_locked and question_count JSON fields without collapsing null
preserve naked-array success and Accept-dependent safe failures
add route delta and OpenAPI migration only after all 11 golden cases pass
acceptance.next_phase4a_work: continue the next catalog-only read after this capability passes full isolated acceptance
